lines.text: Wren's first arrow took the axe out of the headsman's hands. Her second pinned the nearest Hound to the scaffold by his sleeve.
Then Ilse lit Tobin's fog lanterns, all twelve of them, all around the square at once.
White mist rolled over the Square of the Seven. Every Measurer's lens in it fogged at once. So did the Grand Measurer's eyes.
Hold the scaffold! I can't see them! Caddoc!
Vance can freeze a bond by looking at it. But you can't look at what you can't see.
Then the Lowmarket moved. Two thousand people who had been herded there to watch, all deciding at once to stand in the way.
Oswin came up the scaffold steps through the fog with Tobin's glass-steel in his hand. He cut my father's Order chains in two strokes, and the glass in them went dark.
Lord Varr. Your son sends his regards, and says you're to stop being noble and run.
My father stood up on the scaffold, free, in the snow. And for the first time in seventeen years, I think, he stopped being quiet.
Frost burst out of him. The scaffold steps froze solid, and the Hounds climbing them were stuck fast to the knee.
Stop him! He's one old man!
I'm a Rime lord of the old blood, boy. And I have had a very long month.
Caddoc's bought fire hit my father's frost in the middle of the square, and for one long moment the whole Square of the Seven was steam.
Then Tamsin came running through the fog from the College gate, with a boy by one hand and a smaller girl by the other. Lady Sabine's children.
River door! Run! Don't stop for anything!
They ran. Through the fog, through a Lowmarket crowd that opened in front of them and closed behind them like water, and down the Water Stair to the river.
Three black boats with no lights and no banners waited under Mirelle's door. The boatmen wore no colours at all. They were very obviously Corrow's.
Lady Corrow sends her regards. She says you've kidnapped her children, and she'll be furious about it for weeks.
The last thing Wren saw from the boat was Vance on the cathedral steps in the thinning fog. Not shouting. Not running. Just watching them go.
Let them go. I know exactly where they're going.
Half a kingdom away, I felt four threads flare, and burn, and then settle. Steady. Alive. All of them.
Nine days later, my father rode through Greyhollow's gate, and Bram was waiting. They looked at each other like two men who had carried the same heavy thing for fifteen years.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and thirty-two, coming soon.
